content:
maya: quick sync — following up on autoscale globals. main goals: avoid noisy scaling, keep premium p99 latency, and make operator autonomous enough to protect node health.

cj: sounds good. do we have a concrete safety fence idea so operator can refuse harmful prewarms?

maya: yes: operator exposes `veto_reason` + `advice` fields. veto if fragmentation > threshold or MIG boundaries would break packing.

leo: packing rules: operator should return `pack_hint` describing slot shapes that fit best (eg: 4xA100, 2xA100+1xT4). control-plane can then adjust intent.

sasha: agree. also add `prefill_kv: low|medium|high` so we can charge budget accordingly.

amir: question: who throttles repeated prewarm churn? tenants might spam small prewarms.

cj: control-plane maintains per-tenant cooldown + budget. operator enforces a `min_headroom` and will reject if we dip below.

maya: operator should have three modes: log-only, advisory (reject but control-plane can override), enforce. rollout via feature flag.

leo: telemetry: include `recent_prewarms(1h)`, `avg_fill_ms`, `failed_prewarm_count`. these help rate-limit heuristics.

sasha: add `oscillation_score` — a simple EWMA that spikes when tenants flip on/off. operator uses it to lengthen scale-downs.

amir: nice. For MIG fragmentation calc: operator should simulate allocation using current pods & pending intents and return `simulated_success_pct`. control-plane uses that to decide to retry with different shapes.

cj: proto sketch (pseudo):
```
intent_v2 {
  tenant_id: "t-901"
  slots: 6
  preferred_shapes: ["1xA100","2xA100"]
  max_cost_units: 200
  ttl_seconds: 90
}
```
response: `{accepted: bool, veto_reason: "string", pack_hint: ["1xA100"], ready_eta: 45}`

maya: exactly. also operator returns `cost_estimate_units` and `impact_window_seconds` so control-plane can show cost/latency tradeoffs.

leo: about burst fallback: control-plane should include `fallback_policy: allow|deny|require_approval`. operator only enforces pool-level limits, not tenant billing.

sasha: operational detail: operator should never silently drop intents. always respond within X ms with a default deny if overloaded. failing open is dangerous.

amir: agree. define SLA: operator must respond to intent RPC in <= 2s 95th unless `degraded=true`. log degradations.

cj: testing: add sim scenarios for fragmentation-heavy clouds (mixed MIGs), and a 'noisy neighbor' test where many tenants request tiny slots.

maya: add a smoke test that verifies burst fallback path: if veto + fallback allowed -> route to shared-burst and charge credits.

leo: rollout plan: 1) wire operator stub (log-only) -> 2) advisory + metrics dashboard -> 3) soft-enforce for non-prod -> 4) enforce for prod pools. each step 1 week.

sasha: observability: dashboards: prewarm_latency, prewarm_success_rate, veto_rate_by_pool, pack_hint_hit_rate. add alert: veto_rate > 5% for premium for 15m.

amir: security note: intents carry tenant identity. for private installs, sign intents with org key. operator validates signature + nonce. replay window 5m.

maya: ops-bot scheduling: deploy operator-canary with `mode=log-only` to infra-canary-2 at 01:30 UTC.

ops-bot: deploy queued: operator-canary -> infra-canary-2 at 01:30 UTC (ETA 8m).

cj: docs: we need a short "operator-contract.md" explaining RPCs, response codes, instrumentation, and downgrade paths. will draft.

leo: backwards compat: operator accepts both intent_v1 and v2; prefer v2 fields when present. unknown fields ignored.

sasha: last bit: set default `min_headroom=2` for Standard pools, `min_headroom=1` for premium (since premium expects warm slots). we can tune after telemetry.

amir: LGTM. I'll start on signed-intent plumbing.

cj: LGTM, will add sim cases.

maya: thanks. i'll open the follow-up PR with the proto, feature flags, and rollout checklist. lock if no objections in 48h.
